comments.value:
> I mean the biggest benefit of this would be stopping people linking loggers as well.

I've never seen anything like that in a profile yet. I wonder how prevalent that is.

The significant challenge with this suggestion is that it would require VRChat’s team to maintain an ever-changing list of allowed platforms in order to provide users with what they have now, which is a massive undertaking. 

Obviously VRChat’s team, if they were to adopt this suggestion, won't actually do this, and you only need to look at the existing "Trusted URL" scheme for video players, string loaders etc to get a full appreciation that they pick the top 3-4 services and omit everything else, major and minor platforms included. If this were implemented, and there there's a new emerging service that's gaining popularity with certain users today, you'll be lucky to link to it in 3-5 years’ time, if at all.

For this reason, I feel this suggestion will just punish all VRChat's users who, on the whole, quite honestly do the right thing.

Also, this suggestion won't stop people using links for malicious purposes such as location logging, as those who use these services are usually savvy enough to purchase a $5 domain that they can verify ownership of. (See my other reply for an example of this.)

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name} I've seen one user do it in 14k hours on VRChat.

https://vrchat.com/home/user/usr_9057f1f6-7ee5-40cc-ad6b-40b8c436f9c3

If you take a look at their Bio, you'll see a link appears to go to pishock.com, but if you look closer it's actually going to plshock.com (With an imitation front-end) - It's there to log people's locations, and it technically meets the definition of a phishing domain in that it attempts to harvest information from unsuspecting users.

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name} Now I do agree that from scratch a trusted list would be hard to maintain but like I said Discord already has a decent list of trusted platforms that they could use as a start and they can always add onto it as more are available and gain popularity, just like their list they have in their configuration string that grab from their servers for trusted URL for Video, Image, and String Loading so no updates or patches to the core of the game are needed, they just need to do a update to the configuration string then it updates for everyone.

And yes to those that have malicious intentions and the knowledge to buy a domain and verify it, would at least provide some evidence to VRChat that the user knew what the site was and that they were either the owner or had some control over it so if reported could easily take action upon the account for it.

With how easy it has become with code pre-made for web servers on GitHub and sites like https://grabify.link/ so easily accessible I think something if anything needs to be done, it’s too easy now more than ever to make someone click a link and have it grab their info then redirect them to an official site meaning the end user would never notice.

Like I mean let’s be honest yeah you have seen only one in 14k hours but of that how many others have seen that account and not reported it, the link is still there now so think about it, humans are naturally now more intrigued to go to the profile you linked and click on the fake site to see if it’s real, so how many more just from that one comment will now fall into it.

Yeah it won’t stop everything and yeah not everyone will benefit, but with VRChat constantly trying to push their 13+ rating and that the platform is for both kids and adults (That’s a whole other topic we won’t get into) don’t you think they should be at least taking some steps to protect their player base. Especially with the online world as it is at this moment, someone that has been online for a while or even in this game knows they’re people that will go above and beyond to get any little info on people just to scare them.

@{5f2cc099c00297464bd2dd7e|full_name}The lived experience though is that VRChat is terrible at maintaining this sort of thing. I don't care how it could work, I care how it works in practice, and lived experience shows that the idealistic perception you have of their ability to maintain something like this is incredibly unrealistic. 

And again, if you let people DNS validate custom domains, you fix nothing. Period. People who run these will just register custom domains and validate them OR EVEN BETTER, just use the Analytics functionality of linktr.ee and any other allowed services to embed a custom analytics callback or use JavaScript and tracked links via off-site methods on supposedly trusted platforms.

tl;dr: It's a terrible idea, that won't fix the problem, and will severely punish the majority of users - No, no, no. Never. And there's no amount of "Think of the children" talk that will change my mind. 

The only thing I wouldn't mind is the idea of banning users who aren't age-verified from clicking/seeing profile links and or setting them. That would be far, far more preferable to what you're proposing, and it 'protects the children' from being spooked by link tracking.

details:
As creators some of us have custom websites with our own URL that links to us and what we do. And of course with how some users are in VRChat, they try to attempt to clone creators profiles to scam people with one of the biggest comment being “Just look at my website linked to my account. I am the creator!”

I wish there was a way that would check the link, if it was for Discord, YouTube, or any other social then it just be allowed. But any custom domains need to be DNS verified before allowing to be linked to the profile.

(Kinda link how Discord does it would be perfect!)

Not only would this help prevent users being scammed as let’s face it, we sometimes take things at face value and never really investigate it ourselves before we start clicking link but of all things I think it’s gonna make it safer overall.

I mean the biggest benefit of this would be stopping people linking loggers as well. Think about it, of all the players in VRChat only a handful know how to protect themselves online and potentially use a VPN, and with the growing amount of children on the platform that even though someone might not agree with it, it is still happening and they would fall for simply clicking on a link on a profile and then potentially having their information logged and then them threatened with it, and honestly I’m surprised I don’t see it more often.

Yes I know to most it isn’t really something of a priority but I know to those that do take online security at a high value understand where this is actually coming from and where the benefits can be. And of course I would love to hear your possible solutions or ideas on this. But personally I think Discord did it the best with how they verify ownership before you can have them on a profile and I think with having linking any website to a profile on VRChat they should take the same precautions. I mean at the very least if there is a report that someone has been scammed or logged because of these links, you would know who owns it and can potentially take action against that account.
title: Profile Link Verification
